Customer choices

For a household assembling its tax return, capability ccc changes the ways it can handle a recurring matter zzz, whose menu D(z,c)\mathcal D(z,c)D(z,c) includes leaving it unresolved, completing it at home, and purchasing help with different amounts of preparation. Across matters measured by μZ\mu_ZμZ​, each choice has expected benefit UdU_dUd​ after customer time and other nonlabor resources, basic and expert hours jd,edj_d,e_djd​,ed​, and expected qualification transition mdm_dmd​ assigned to an eligible novice.

With basic time available at outside wage bbb, expert time priced at www, and complete practice payments valued at Δ\DeltaΔ, competitive fees follow the expression above. Adding the novice’s payment Δmd\Delta m_dΔmd​ to the customer fee exactly covers the provider’s labor bill, giving the learning credit a financing source before it enters the customer’s optimization.

Between two modes for the same matter, a higher expert wage gives greater weight to the hours each uses, while a higher qualification value gives greater weight to the learning each supplies. Even with customer capability fixed, these prices can change which file the household submits, connecting the service-demand and practice schedules to the evolving professional market.

Private study

For a novice learning to handle later client matters independently, qualification opens future expert earnings and has portable value Δ=VE−VN\Delta=V_E-V_NΔ=VE​−VN​, while obsolescence returns experts to novice status at rate δ>0\delta>0δ>0. Purchasing study intensity x≥0x\ge0x≥0 at cost κx2/2\kappa x^2/2κx2/2 gives expected gain xΔ−κx2/2x\Delta-\kappa x^2/2xΔ−κx2/2, whose maximizer on the positive-value region supplies the study choice in the first equation.

Practice arrives at per-novice rate M/(1−E)M/(1-E)M/(1−E), and paying Δ\DeltaΔ per successful transition cancels its private capital gain inside the novice’s value equation. Subtracting that equation from the expert’s equation leaves the wage premium, obsolescence, discounting, and optimized study surplus, producing the qualification-value law while practice remains present in physical accumulation.

Over a short interval, purchased study gives each novice a transition probability proportional to xxx, whose expected gain is the probability times the value of qualification. Multiplying that individual intensity by the novice share gives formal entry, while multiplying obsolescence by the expert share gives qualification loss, so both sides of accumulation count population transitions in the same units.

We measure EEE as a qualified population share, MMM as an aggregate transition flow, xxx as individual study intensity, and Δ\DeltaΔ as discounted career value, so the entry equation counts the people who actually acquire the assessed ability. Each qualified person supplies one expert clock hour per unit of time, connecting the resulting population to available service hours and, in the shared-expertise extension, to research labor.

Long-run entry

When the material retained for junior learning changes while the remaining expert work in purchased files stays fixed, we obtain the diagnostic-portfolio comparison by keeping the selected modes within their strict purchase margins. Its inverse wage w(E)>bw(E)>bw(E)>b is independent of MMM and Δ\DeltaΔ, and a continuous nonincreasing wage schedule gives weakly decreasing individual study and strictly decreasing aggregate formal transitions T(E)=(1−E)x(E)T(E)=(1-E)x(E)T(E)=(1−E)x(E), since the novice population also contracts as EEE rises.

Positive qualification drift at the lower feasible endpoint and negative drift at the upper endpoint give a unique stationary population for each practice flow in the comparison interval. At two such equilibria, subtracting their accumulation identities gives T1−T0=(M0−M1)−δ(E0−E1)T^1-T^0=(M^0-M^1)-\delta(E^0-E^1)T1−T0=(M0−M1)−δ(E0−E1), so a practice loss lowers expertise and induces strictly positive, incomplete formal replacement.

For a differentiable wage, the denominator Λ=δ+x−(1−E)wE/[κ(R+x)]\Lambda=\delta+x-(1-E)w_E/[\kappa(R+x)]Λ=δ+x−(1−E)wE​/[κ(R+x)] gives EM=1/ΛE_M=1/\LambdaEM​=1/Λ and replacement fraction −TM=1−δ/Λ-T_M=1-\delta/\Lambda−TM​=1−δ/Λ. Because Λ>δ\Lambda>\deltaΛ>δ, this fraction lies strictly between zero and one, with its magnitude determined jointly by study costs, obsolescence, and the equilibrium wage response.

Increasing expertise affects this balance through more people losing qualification, fewer novices able to acquire it, and a weaker study incentive wherever the wage falls. Together those responses determine how strongly net entry declines with the population, which is why their common denominator converts a change in practice into a change in stationary expertise.

Fees and validation

Expert services

Dulleck and Kerschbamer (2006) studies diagnosis and treatment when customers have difficulty assessing expert services, motivating the joint account of fees and reliability.

For a household deciding whether to purchase advice, both the fee and the risk of an unresolved mistake matter, as the credence-goods analysis of Dulleck and Kerschbamer (2006) explains. Within our extension, fixed franchises face isoelastic demand with ε>1\varepsilon>1ε>1. Generalized price PPP combines the fee with the certainty-equivalent loss from error. Each case uses generation time e(c)e(c)e(c), checking time vvv, and resources k(c)k(c)k(c). Its error probability π(c)e−v\pi(c)e^{-v}π(c)e−v declines as experts validate the work.

With constant absolute risk aversion γ\gammaγ and error loss LLL, the certainty-equivalent cost is rγ(z)=γ−1log⁡[1+z(eγL−1)]r_\gamma(z)=\gamma^{-1}\log[1+z(e^{\gamma L}-1)]rγ​(z)=γ−1log[1+z(eγL−1)], whose risk-neutral limit is LzLzLz. Optimized generalized unit cost T\mathcal TT enters the isoelastic markup shown above, and its wage derivative counts the expert hours needed per completed case, giving aggregate demand DS=TwN(c)P−εD_S=\mathcal T_w N(c)P^{-\varepsilon}DS​=Tw​N(c)P−ε.

For risk-neutral customers, optimal checking is v∗=[log⁡(Lπ(c)/w)]+v^*=[\log(L\pi(c)/w)]_+v∗=[log(Lπ(c)/w)]+​, so more reliable files reduce validation at a fixed wage while a larger possible loss raises its return. Lemma F.1 proves that the resulting expert demand decreases strictly with the wage, including the points at which validation enters or leaves the selected service.

At an interior checking choice, the marginal reduction in expected error loss equals the wage paid for the additional expert time. More reliable household material reduces that marginal benefit at the old checking intensity, while greater potential loss raises it, carrying the content and consequences of a submitted file into the amount of professional review purchased.

Research production

Research difficulty

Bloom et al. (2020) documents rising research effort alongside declining research productivity across several settings, motivating explicit difficulty in producing the next advance.

Extending the service economy to a field with expertise shared by customer work and research introduces completed research packets alongside client cases. Positive coefficients vRv_RvR​ and mRm_RmR​ preserve each method’s validation stage, while qqq prices computation and ξ\xiξ measures its use per human research hour, so human packets require aHa_HaH​ expert hours and autonomous packets require aMa_MaM​ computation units.

Expert clearing joins customer services to human research, whose fixed expenditure flow BRB_RBR​ purchases labor and computation. Across industries, products, and firms, Bloom et al. (2020) documents rising research effort alongside declining research productivity, motivating our explicit difficulty term A−ϕA^{-\phi}A−ϕ, which reduces the frontier increment supplied by a completed packet as AAA grows.

For the selected service portfolio, C(c)=C0eγcC(c)=C_0e^{\gamma c}C(c)=C0​eγc and DS=C(c)w−εD_S=C(c)w^{-\varepsilon}DS​=C(c)w−ε translate discovery and preparation into purchased expert hours, while M(c)=M0e−βccM(c)=M_0e^{-\beta_c c}M(c)=M0​e−βc​c follows diagnostic transitions as customer capability grows. Multiplying aMa_MaM​ by a positive factor changes the computation needed for both stages of the machine method, giving customer use and research production separate ways to alter the shared economy.

Market clearing determines today’s wage from the inherited population and the feasible research methods, while the career equations connect that wage to the earnings expected over the remaining horizon. Following both conditions together gives a path in which customer preparation changes current work and the value of becoming able to perform future work.

Procurement compares packet costs at the wage supporting the allocation, determining the research method and its labor cost together (fig. 6). Changing expertise or customer demand moves the clearing roots, which can carry the economy across a method boundary while research requirements remain fixed.
